To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified and quantified novel biofluid markers that are sensitive and specific to LRRK2 inhibitor exposure and that these biofluid markers are consistent with pharmacodynamic markers of LRRK inhibition.

three brain-penetrating LRRK2 inhibitors were administered in cynomolgus monkeys at different doses, and that LRRK2 pharmacodynamic markers were measured in biofluids to determine their pharmacodynamic properties.

three different LRRK2 inhibitors reduced LRRK kinase activity in the brain, as measured by reduced pS935 and pS1292 LRRK2, in the blood, as measured by decreased pS935 LRRK2 in mononuclear cells; and in the periphery, as measured by a reduction in exosome LRR2 and docosahexaenoic acid levels in the urine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a panel of pharmacodynamic markers that can be used to assess LRRK2 inhibitor potency and efficacy in the clinic.
the development of pharmacodynamic biomarkers for assessing the efficacy of LRRK-kinase inhibitors.
the development of biomarkers for LRRK-kinase inhibitors in blood and biofluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these pharmacodynamic markers of LRRK inhibition are useful for assessing drug efficacy in the brain and peripheral organs.
these pharmacodynamic markers of LRRK kinase inhibition in blood, urine and CSF are robust and reproducible in the cynomolgus monkey model.

these data provide evidence of the potential of LRRK inhibitors as a treatment for LRRK-associated neurodegenerative disorders, and the potential of these pharmacodynamic markers to monitor LRRK2 activity in the brain and peripheral tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LRRK2 inhibitors reduce LRRK2 levels in exosomes in the urine and CSF, and this may represent an important pharmacodynamic marker for the brain-penetrance of LRRK inhibitors in humans.
the combination of blood, urine and CSF biomarkers provides a comprehensive picture of LRRK kinase inhibition and LRRK2 exosomal protein levels in the periphery and CNS.
LRRK2 inhibitors reduce the levels of LRR2 in exosomes in the blood, urine and CSF and that these changes can be used as pharmacodynamic markers for LRR2 inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LRRK2 activity is inhibited in blood, urine, CSF, and exosomes following administration of selective LRRK inhibitors, and the magnitude of inhibition is dose dependent.
the LRRK2 inhibitor-induced reduction in LRRK2 secretion in exosomes can be used to monitor LRRK2 activity in biofluids.

LRRK2 inhibitors can be detected in the urine and CSF of cynomolgous macaques, and these can be used as biomarkers to assess LRRK2 inhibitor potency in the brain and the periphery, and to guide dosing strategies.
